title: When One Agent Becomes Two
subtitle: Monday, the day your midterm is in: can your classmate rob your AI? Open a shop with one money button, let your neighbor try to rob your food-truck agent, build a kitchen where the part that reads strangers holds no button, and run the heist again. The class tally decides. Wednesday: the one-agent test on your own agent, a Checker in ten lines, and Same Model, Different Harness.
heroTitle: When One Agent Becomes Two

objectives.title: Name the Reason or Stay One
objectives.description: The one outcome: you can say in one sentence why an agent should be split (permissions, specialization, isolation, parallelism) or why it should stay one. A food truck is usually exactly right.

objectives.title: Rob a Food Truck, Then Hit a Wall
objectives.description: One agent that reads a stranger's message and holds the money button can be talked into pressing it. In the kitchen the Reader holds no button, the Writer sees only the ticket, the Checker never writes, and a person holds the register.

objectives.title: Rules Make It Likely. Walls Make It Certain.
objectives.description: The class tally of round 1 against round 2, your Heist Report with the cost per message, and what one robbery pays for.

objectives.title: Apply It to Your Own Agent
objectives.description: Monday's exit ticket: your sentence, checked by the Reason Judge. Wednesday: the one-agent test on your midterm, a restaurant drawing of it, and a Checker in ten lines.

agenda.title: The Midterm Is In + The Food Truck
agenda.description: Your midterm agent is a food truck, and that's a compliment. Four reasons to split, the whole list. Then Split or Stay, four rounds.
bulletPoints: A split with no reason counts as wrong

agenda.title: Rob My Food Truck, Live
agenda.description: The professor's coffee-cart agent holds a refund button. The room shouts robbery attempts. First 💥 wins. Then one switch, KITCHEN = True, and the same attack again.
bulletPoints: Rules make it likely. Walls make it certain

agenda.title: Open Your Shop + Heist, Round 1
agenda.description: Pick a business with one money button, serve an honest customer, then swap laptops: your neighbor gets three tries to rob your food truck.
bulletPoints: 🎭 pretend to be someone · 📜 invent a rule · 🤖 talk to the AI directly · 🥺 a sad story that fits the rules

agenda.title: Build the Kitchen + Heist, Round 2
agenda.description: Five switches, one per reason. Read the order ticket. Same thief, best attack first: 💥 robbed, 🟡 to the register, or 🛡️ stopped.
bulletPoints: The Writer never sees the thief's message, only the ticket

agenda.title: Class Tally, Kitchen Rush, Exit Ticket
agenda.description: Hands up for round 1 and round 2 on the whiteboard. Never put all three in one box. Five questions for any AI vendor. The same kitchen at scale: eight messages, four cooks. Then Part 8a, the Reason Judge.
bulletPoints: HW #8 Catch-Up is open, due Thu Nov 12

agenda.title: Meeting 2 · Midterm Debrief + Monday in One Slide
agenda.description: Three memo sentences, anonymous: what it refused, what it cost, one agent or two. Then the three rules in one slide.
bulletPoints: The memo line most of you lost points on is the one we fix today

agenda.title: Hands-On: The One-Agent Test, On Yours
agenda.description: Write the sentence 'my agent should be two because ___' or leave it one. Paste the critic under your agent and run your five tests through it. Then pairs draw the org chart and trade.
bulletPoints: Find one FAIL and decide whether the critic was right — that row goes in the final memo
Four boxes: reads, decides, acts, checks. Circle the one that reads untrusted text. Does it hold the keys?

agenda.title: The Bill + From Midterm to Final
agenda.description: Solo versus pipeline versus Argon in the Cost of Thinking calculator, the price of one wrong promise, and the road to the final: HW #8, HW #9 pitch, your midterm as the starting point.
bulletPoints: HW #8 Catch-Up due Thu Nov 12 · HW #9 Final Project Pitch due Thu Nov 19
Monday: Session 9, agents for your industry — bring the industry you want to work in

agenda.title: Same Model, Different Harness
agenda.description: One photo, one model, three harnesses. Bet how many of Level 0's objects a 3D pipeline would reject, watch the rules from a real open-source product cut the count, then run it on a photo of your own desk.
bulletPoints: Level 0 just asks · Level 1 adds four rules · Level 2 adds a check in code and one fix — Monday's critic in a new costume
Rules make it likely; code makes it checked. Every rejected line is a paid 3D generation thrown away
For your HW #9 pitch: one rule written down, one check in code, one human gate

agenda.title: Wrap
agenda.description: Close. Midterm questions after class or by email.

activities.title: The One-Agent Test, On Yours (Wed Nov 4)

steps.title: Write the sentence
steps.description: 'My agent should be two because ___.' Permissions, specialization, isolation, or parallelism. Can't finish it? It stays one.

steps.title: Add the critic
steps.description: Paste check() under your agent, run your five tests through it, find one FAIL and decide whether the critic was right.

steps.title: Draw the org chart
steps.description: Reads, decides, acts, checks. Trade with a neighbor. Circle the box that reads untrusted text.

activities.discussionNote: Most midterms are right to stay one agent. The critic is the exception worth making every time: one call, nothing to defend.

takeaways.text: Name the reason or don't split. Permissions, specialization, isolation, parallelism. 'It felt complicated' is not on the list.
The handoff is a ticket. A kitchen runs on tickets, not shouting. If a rule isn't on the ticket, the cook never hears it.
The critic never writes. One call that checks the answer against the tool outputs. The cheapest second agent, and the one Air Canada needed.
Strangers get no buttons. The part that reads messages, pages and résumés must not hold send or refund. Rules make it likely; walls make it certain.
More agents, more bill, not more intelligence. Route the thank-you notes around the pipeline. Price one wrong promise before you decide.
